content.title: Information about the FrontLine Farming lease at Majestic View Nature Center
content.summary: FrontLine Farming has leased 1.83 acres at Majestic View Nature Center since 2019 for agricultural and community activities, but the City of Arvada has decided to terminate this lease due to ongoing compliance, operational, and safety concerns, including an unauthorized electrical installation discovered in March 2026. The City emphasizes that this decision was not made to repurpose the land or expand programming, but rather to ensure the safety of public spaces, particularly those used by children and families. City officials are committed to managing the transition respectfully and responsibly through the end of the growing season.
content.body:
FrontLine Farming has leased approximately 1.83 acres (420 feet by 190 feet) of City-owned property at Majestic View Nature Center since 2019 for agricultural production and community programming. The Frontline Farming agricultural lease area is located at 7000 Garrison St. on the [southeastern-most portion of the Majestic View Nature Center property](https://www.arvadaco.gov/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=7629), just south of the Nature Center’s outdoor classroom and nature play area.

The City of Arvada recognizes and appreciates the contributions FrontLine Farming has made to the community over the past seven seasons through food production, education and community engagement. We understand that many community members care deeply about this partnership and have questions about the City's decision to terminate the lease.

We want to clarify that this decision was not made to expand children's programming, construct new facilities, repurpose the farm site for another use, or sell the property. The City also has no plans to use the leased farming area differently. The decision was based on a series of documented lease compliance, operational and safety concerns that were addressed with the organization over an extended period of time.

“This has been a difficult situation, and one we did not arrive at lightly. We value the work FrontLine Farming has done in the community and the relationships built over time. At the same time, the City has a responsibility to ensure that public spaces — especially those used by children and families — are safe and operated in accordance with established agreements,” said [Ryan Stevenson, Director of the City’s Vibrant Community and Neighborhoods](https://www.arvadaco.gov/196/Vibrant-Community-and-Neighborhoods).

“Despite ongoing efforts to work through concerns, we were not able to find a sustainable path forward. We remain committed to managing this transition through the growing season at the end of the fall in a way that is respectful, responsible and mindful of the community.”

Beginning in 2025, City staff documented concerns related to lease compliance, use of City property outside the leased area, required reporting, property maintenance, and coordination of activities on the site. These concerns were addressed through meetings, site visits, emails, verbal conversations and a [formal notice issued in May 2025](https://www.arvadaco.gov/DocumentCenter/View/7624/FrontLine-Farming-May-2025-Lease-Agreement-Violations-Letter) that provided an opportunity to correct identified issues.

Following the May 2025 violation notice, City staff continued to document lease compliance and operational concerns while working with FrontLine Farming leadership through meetings, site visits, emails, and ongoing communication to address those issues.

A significant factor in the City's decision to exercise the termination clause in the lease was the discovery of an unauthorized electrical installation on City-owned property in March 2026. The wiring originated from a City-owned electrical panel and [extended more than 150 feet through portions of the Majestic View Outdoor Classroom and Nature Play area](https://www.arvadaco.gov/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=7628) before reaching the leased farm area. City staff determined that the installation had not been permitted, had not been approved by the City, and did not comply with applicable electrical code requirements.

The wiring was discovered when a City employee performing maintenance work in the Outdoor Classroom unknowingly came within inches of striking a concealed wire with a pickaxe. Following the discovery, City electricians and safety personnel investigated the installation and removed the wiring due to concerns about employee safety, public safety and the proximity of the installation to areas regularly used by children, volunteers staff and visitors.

The City understands that reasonable people may have differing perspectives about this decision. However, the City has a responsibility to manage public property safely, ensure compliance with lease agreements and maintain environments that are appropriate for their intended public use.

Although the lease is being terminated, the City is allowing FrontLine Farming to continue operations through the current growing season, ending in November 2026. The City remains committed to working professionally and respectfully with FrontLine Farming during this transition period and appreciates the positive contributions the organization has made to the community.

### [FrontLine Farming Lease FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=111)

[Why is the City terminating FrontLine Farming's lease?](#)
:   The City’s decision was based on a series of documented lease compliance, operational, and safety concerns that were addressed with FrontLine Farming over an extended period of time. Beginning in 2025, City staff documented concerns related to lease compliance, use of City property outside the leased area, required reporting, property maintenance, coordination of activities on the site, and other operational issues. These concerns were addressed through meetings, site visits, emails, verbal conversations, and a formal notice issued in May 2025.

    A significant factor in the City’s decision was the discovery of an unauthorized electrical installation connected to City-owned infrastructure that crossed portions of the Outdoor Classroom and Nature Play area. City staff determined the installation had not been approved by the City, had not been permitted, and did not comply with applicable electrical code requirements.

[Is the City terminating the lease to expand children’s programming?](#)
:   No, the City is not terminating the lease to expand children's programming.

    While the electrical installation was discovered in an area used by children and families, the decision was based on lease compliance, operational, and safety concerns—not a desire to expand programming.

[Is the City planning to build something else on the property?](#)
:   No, the City currently has no plans to build new facilities, expand existing facilities, or repurpose the leased farming area for another use.

[Is the City planning to sell the land?](#)
:   No, the City has no plans to sell the leased farming area. The property remains part of the Majestic View Nature Center site.

[Does the City manage any other leases of public land for agricultural purposes?](#)
:   Yes, the City has three other similar lease agreements throughout Arvada with GoFarm, the Arvada Community Garden, and Rose Roots Community Garden. An overview of how the City manages these partnerships to support community food access was included in an article on [page 6 of the February/March 2026 Arvada Report](https://mcclibraryfunctions.azurewebsites.us/api/munidocDownload/31089/92a5dc347299e/pdf).

[Was FrontLine Farming given notice before the lease was terminated?](#)
:   Yes, in May 2025, the City issued a formal notice identifying lease compliance concerns and providing an opportunity to correct those issues.

    Over the following year, City staff continued working with FrontLine Farming through meetings, emails, site visits, and ongoing communication regarding lease compliance and operational concerns.

[Did the City attempt to work with FrontLine Farming before terminating the lease?](#)
:   Yes, City staff spent approximately a year attempting to address concerns through meetings, site visits, emails, verbal conversations, coordination efforts, and a formal notice process. The City sought to clarify expectations, improve communication, coordinate activities on the property, and resolve concerns without immediately terminating the lease.

[Was the electrical installation the only reason the lease was terminated?](#)
:   No, the electrical installation was a significant factor in the City’s decision, but it was not the only concern.

    The City had documented lease compliance, operational, and property management concerns prior to the discovery of the electrical installation. The electrical issue became the most serious concern because of the safety risks involved and its location near areas regularly used by children, volunteers, staff, and visitors.

[What was the issue with the electrical installation?](#)
:   In March 2026, City staff discovered an unauthorized electrical installation connected to City-owned infrastructure.

    The wiring originated from a City-owned electrical panel and extended more than 150 feet through portions of the Outdoor Classroom and Nature Play area before reaching the leased farm area.

    City staff determined the installation:

    - Had not been approved by the City.
    - Had not been permitted.
    - Did not comply with applicable electrical code requirements.

    The wiring was removed following an investigation by City staff and electricians.

[Is FrontLine Farming being forced to leave immediately?](#)
:   No, the City is allowing FrontLine Farming to continue operating through the current growing season, ending in November 2026. This allows the organization to complete the growing season, continue serving the community, and plan for its next location.

[Where can I review the documents related to this decision?](#)
:   The City has published the following materials related to the lease:

    - [City of Arvada’s 2019 lease agreement with FrontLine Farming](https://www.arvadaco.gov/DocumentCenter/View/7631/Agreement_-Lease_-Front-Line-Farming_-Agricultural-Production-at-the-Majestic-View-Nature-Center)
